title: Add persistent per-workspace isolation
description: Add an Isolate workspace setting and workspace-list indicator. Route every workspace connection, including local terminals, through one persistent platform-specific isolate per workspace. Preserve a future boundary for workspace network attachment. macOS uses Apple Containerization through a native helper, Linux targets a lightweight microVM runtime, and Windows targets WSL-based isolation.
notes:
2026-09-01 implementation slice: added a durable Terminal isolation (Preview) setting with configurable validated host mounts, a workspace-tile box badge, one process-coordinated persistent isolate lease per workspace, atomic bundle-import/edit/open occupancy protection, and shutdown/update race guards. macOS bootstrap uses a deterministic Apple Containerization container and routes local plus explicitly insecure brokerless SSH terminals through it. Runtime availability is advertised only when the supported Apple host and container executable are both present. The persistent environment is stopped, not deleted, so installed guest packages survive. Preview is intentionally fail-closed for verified SSH, credentials, Docker/WSL, non-terminal workspace clients, unsupported platforms, and missing runtime. Definition deletion warns that persistent runtime cleanup is not implemented. Full check passed: zero-warning Release build; 6,946 tests passed and 4 explicitly opt-in integration tests skipped. Parent remains in progress for signed native helper, every-client routing and workspace networking, reset/delete lifecycle, verified SSH and credential bridges, Linux, and Windows backends.
Post-rebase verification against origin/main: the full gate passed again with 6,949 tests passed and 4 explicitly opt-in integration tests skipped; the three additional passes are upstream remote-startup regressions.
2026-09-01 correction: replaced the invented Terminal isolation (Preview) product scope with the requested workspace-level Isolate workspace control. Workspaces settings now show a labeled isolation toggle on every workspace row, and the editor has a dedicated Isolation section immediately after Appearance. Enabling isolation no longer creates any implicit host/home/PATH mount; mounts are user-created only, starting with a blank host source, /workspace guest path, and read-only access. Compatible Apple-silicon macOS 26 hosts missing the container CLI now show an Install Apple container action that opens Apple's official latest signed-installer release. Updated the workspace tile and delete-dialog language, ADR, persistence/occupancy tests, UI contracts, and installer composition tests. Rendered the Workspaces settings page for visual verification. Full gate passed: warning-free Release build; 6,957 tests passed and 4 explicitly opt-in integration tests skipped.
2026-09-01 UI correction: the workspace editor's Isolation section now names the missing macOS runtime as Apple container and includes an in-place Install Apple container action wired to the existing official release flow. Runtime identity is supplied by the platform installer rather than hard-coded as a generic 'supported runtime'. Replaced the two raw notice elements with SettingsRow components, eliminating the overlap in the reported screen. Rendered settings-workspace-editor at 1440x1200 to verify the result. Full gate passed: zero-warning Release build; 6,959 tests passed and 4 explicitly opt-in integration tests skipped.
2026-09-01 copy correction: the Apple container prompts now say it is needed only to enable workspace isolation, rather than presenting it as an app-wide requirement. The workspace editor now explains the model: one persistent environment per workspace, shared by its connections including local terminals, with packages and guest files retained between sessions and host access limited to explicitly configured mounts. Rendered both Workspaces settings and the workspace editor to verify wrapping and layout. Full gate passed: zero-warning Release build; 6,959 tests passed and 4 explicitly opt-in integration tests skipped.
2026-09-02 runtime/lifecycle correction: stopped Apple container services are now started automatically with container system start and re-probed instead of surfacing “runtime is not running.” Opening an isolated workspace moves it to the foreground immediately and shows a full-window “Starting Apple container…” loading state until its persistent isolate is ready. Running workspaces—including Main—keep the isolation toggle enabled; changing it requires the explicit “Workspace will be restarted to change isolation configuration” confirmation, closes with that confirmed decision, persists the setting, and reopens the workspace. The workspace editor uses the same restart path while host-mount editing remains locked for running workspaces. The rail's cube badge now has a tile-color mask so the main workspace glyph cannot show through it. Full gate passed: warning-free Release build; 6,962 tests passed and 4 explicitly opt-in integration tests skipped.

First-start follow-up: Apple container startup passes --enable-kernel-install so an installed runtime without a configured default guest kernel completes setup non-interactively under the same loading state.
2026-09-02 first-run timeout correction: reproduced the failure against Apple container 1.3.1 on this Mac. The 664 MB recommended kernel took 165 seconds, crossing the previous two-minute process timeout and leaving the API running with kernel installation cancelled. Runtime preparation now executes Apple container system start as an idempotent readiness step every time, uses the CLI's 180-second API-service timeout, and applies no app wall-clock timeout to kernel installation. Workspace image pulling is a separate no-wall-clock-timeout step using plain progress; create is bounded to five minutes, container lifecycle to two minutes, and probes to ten seconds. The full-window loader now displays live service, kernel download percentage, verification, unpacking, image download percentage, create, start, and validation phases. Added an opt-in native provider integration test that creates a real isolate, executes its shell, verifies root persistence across stop/start, and deletes only its test container. Ran it explicitly twice against the installed runtime; both passed and no test containers remain. Full gate passed with a zero-warning Release build: 6,963 tests passed and 5 opt-in integration tests skipped.
2026-09-02 mount-restart correction: host mounts remain editable while a workspace is open. Saving a changed mount set uses the existing explicit restart confirmation, closes the workspace, saves, and reopens it. Apple container mount configuration is creation-time only, so the provider stops the isolate, exports its complete writable root, builds a deterministic workspace-state OCI image, recreates the same named container with the new mounts, then starts and validates it. Export and build are cancellable but have no wall-clock timeout; each lifecycle phase is displayed in the full-window startup state. Unit/integration coverage includes restart orchestration, command ordering/timeouts, rollback attempt, and snapshot-image validation. The opt-in native macOS test passed against Apple container 1.3.1, preserving /root and an executable installed under /usr/local/bin across two mount replacements while proving the removed host mount is not copied into the guest. Full gate passed: warning-free Release build; 6,964 tests passed and 5 opt-in/external integration tests skipped.
2026-09-02 runtime-image correction: newly created Apple Container isolates now use a pinned official Ubuntu 24.04 arm64 image instead of Alpine. Workspace Isolation settings persist an optional OCI image reference per workspace; blank selects the Ubuntu default. Changing the image while a workspace is open uses the existing restart confirmation with an explicit warning that installed packages and guest-only files are removed, pulls without a wall-clock timeout, recreates the same named isolate with its configured mounts, then starts and validates it. Legacy Alpine isolates are preserved when no explicit image is selected, avoiding destructive migration. OpenSSH bootstrap supports apt-based Ubuntu images and legacy apk images. The native Apple Container integration test passed against the real runtime and verified Ubuntu identity, root persistence, and mount reconfiguration. The complete full gate passed after fixing a recovery-path regression discovered by the first run.

acceptance_criteria: Strict and AcceptNew SSH work without host-network preflight; unknown and changed keys use the existing explicit review UX; approved keys are written atomically with owner-only guest permissions under a mount-protected path; concurrent connections cannot overwrite another connection's trust; tests cover unknown, trusted, changed, cancellation, restart persistence, and future workspace-network routing.

title: Fix cold native release artifact publication
description: v0.1.18 release run 33253068402 compiled the native terminal runtime on a cache miss but macOS Bash aborted at the empty dotnet_artifacts_arguments array expansion, so native/artifacts/osx-arm64 was never published and the release failed. Use Bash 3-safe optional-array expansion, add a regression contract test, run the full gate, and publish a replacement build.
notes:
v0.1.25 release run 33268645627 passed all real gates but the release job failed twice after libghostty verification because build-terminal-font-assets.sh invoked Asura.Packaging without the configured external artifacts path. The sealed release source correctly denied creation of tools/Asura.Packaging/obj. Routed the nested publisher through ASURA_BUILD_ARTIFACTS_ROOT, matching the libghostty and CEF builders, and added an architecture contract test. Full repository gate passes.
v0.1.26 release run 33272619331 proved the font/.NET routing fix: libghostty and terminal font assets built successfully from sealed source. It then exposed the same boundary violation in the SQL worker: Maven clean tried to delete native/sql-language-worker/target under the read-only source. Added a configurable Maven build directory, route local release builds to ASURA_BUILD_ARTIFACTS_ROOT/sql-language-worker/<rid>, updated every local build/legal/smoke path, removed CI's obsolete writable target exception, and added an architecture contract. A real Maven package build from a read-only source copy with external output passed and left no source target directory.
v0.1.27 release run 33276642168 passed dependency evidence, native terminal packaging, Release build, format/architecture, and every other test shard. The core shard exposed a macOS NamedPipeServerStream teardown race: WaitForConnectionAsync could surface an internal NullReferenceException after cancellation and disposal. ServeAsync now treats any exception observed only after the coordinator's shutdown token is cancelled as teardown completion; pre-shutdown failures retain existing behavior. Strengthened disposal coverage to 32 cycles. Local evidence before push: exact two-test regression run passed; 100 fresh test processes passed (200/200 invocations); ./scripts/check.sh --full passed.
v0.1.28 release run 33278743882 passed every dependency/build/architecture/test job, including the macOS pipe regression, and completed all sealed native payload builders. Assemble macOS application then failed immediately in package-macos.sh because Bash 3.2 with set -u rejects the empty local identity_arguments array expansion before the first sealed-source verification. Replaced every optional identity/.NET artifacts expansion in package-macos.sh with the established Bash-3-safe form and added an architecture contract covering both arrays. Local Bash 3.2 evidence reproduces the old expression (exit 127, unbound variable) and passes the safe expression (exit 0); focused regression passes. Complete local package assembly reaches the full-Xcode icon compiler, which is the first unavailable local prerequisite because this machine has only CommandLineTools and no Developer ID/notary profile.
Final local pre-push evidence for the Bash packaging fix: ./scripts/check.sh --full passed; package-macos.sh with both optional arrays empty validated the full 247-file CEF runtime and advanced to the expected full-Xcode prerequisite, with no unbound-variable failure. No Xcode.app or local Developer ID/notary profile exists, so adaptive icon compilation, Developer ID signing, and notarization can only execute on the configured macOS release runner.
v0.1.29 release run 33282227730 passed all prerequisite jobs, the sealed native payload build, Xcode 26 icon compilation, and the Bash-3-safe sealed-source verification/build path. It then failed because MacOsProductIdentity accepted a synthetic RATC marker while actual Xcode Assets.car archives use the 8-byte BOMStore signature. Local evidence: the first 500 Apple-shipped Assets.car files found under /System all begin BOMStore; no RATC catalogs were found. Updated the validator and fixtures to BOMStore, required a 16-byte minimum, and added a regression rejecting the legacy fake RATC marker. Three focused bundle-builder tests pass.
v0.1.30 release run 33285596302 passed every prerequisite job, sealed native payload builds, real Xcode 26 asset compilation, full app publish, Developer ID signing, notarization, stapling, and Gatekeeper assessment. The final signing-evidence step failed because codesign parses a space-separated --extract-certificates prefix as an input path. Local /usr/bin/codesign reproduction against Calculator.app: the old form exits 1 with '<prefix>: No such file or directory'; --extract-certificates=<prefix> exits 0 and writes the full certificate chain. Changed sign-notarize-macos.sh to pass the option atomically and added an acceptance contract regression.
v0.1.31 release run 33289086966 proved the atomic codesign certificate extraction fix: Developer ID signing, notarization, stapling, Gatekeeper assessment, and certificate extraction all passed. The next command failed because macOS 26 plutil cannot insert into a JSON plist and reports 'Conversion to OpenStep format is not supported.' Local reproduction matches exactly. Signing evidence now builds as XML, inserts all typed fields, explicitly converts to JSON, and an executable macOS regression verifies JsonDocument can parse it. Downstream audit found and fixed the same space-separated --extract-certificates bug in NativeMacVerifier before it could fail during security-campaign evidence assembly.
v0.1.32 release run 33292596942 did not reach release assembly because the hosted app shard exposed the agent-chat initial-scroll race tracked in asura-w1w. The packaging/notarization fixes remain locally green; no rerun was used.
v0.1.33 run 33294547940 passed dependency evidence, all test shards (including the deterministic agent-history regression), Release build, format/architecture, sealed native payloads, Xcode app assembly, Developer ID signing, notarization, stapling, Gatekeeper, archiving, and archive re-verification. Exact release-candidate evidence then rejected the signed libghostty-vt because its pre-sign build receipt records the linker-signed dylib length/hash while Developer ID codesign necessarily replaces the Mach-O signature and changes both. Local exact reproduction: a linker-signed arm64 dylib grew from 16,792 to 34,832 bytes under codesign. Keep strict receipt byte/hash validation before signing; after deep signature, certificate, stapler, and Gatekeeper verification, validate immutable receipt metadata and record the exact signed dylib as its own campaign component.
Fix local evidence: the executable macOS regression uses /usr/bin/codesign on a copied Mach-O binary, verifies the pre-sign bytes match the receipt, verifies codesign changes the digest and reproduces strict validation failure, then verifies the post-sign contract. It passed 10/10 fresh processes. The release verifier now completes deep codesign, expected certificate/team, stapler, and Gatekeeper verification before post-sign native metadata validation; strict byte/hash validation remains in MacOsAppBundleBuilder before signing; the exact signed libghostty-vt hash is added to campaign components. ./scripts/check.sh --quick and ./scripts/check.sh --full both pass locally (warning-free Release build, 246 accessibility/security tests, 1,748 app tests, 470 architecture tests, and all remaining suites).

title: Route every isolated workspace client through its network boundary
description: Extend isolation beyond terminal launch planning. Browser, file, database, Git, Docker, process/statistics, agent, diagnostics, and other workspace-scoped clients must consume an isolate-scoped transport or fail closed. Implement app/workspace proxy overrides plus WireGuard, OpenVPN, OpenConnect/AnyConnect, and Tailscale attachment; retain proxy-environment injection for non-isolated local terminals.

notes:
Architecture trace on 2026-09-02: terminal launch is the only current workspace-aware execution path. InMemorySessionHostClient and its browser/file/database/Docker/Git/monitor factories are application singletons; agent provider HTTP and MCP runtimes are also host-owned. A guest-wide implementation therefore requires an out-of-process per-workspace session host (or equivalent guest RPC service), with SessionOwner.WorkspaceId selecting its endpoint. Merely injecting proxy variables would not cover ADO.NET/raw TCP, local filesystem/process monitoring, Docker, Chromium, or MCP subprocesses. Until that guest host exists, do not describe those clients as routed and do not add silent host fallback. Image selection/default Ubuntu work is being landed separately under asura-1be; this issue remains open for the full execution boundary plus later proxy/VPN/Tailscale attachment.
2026-09-02 boundary enforcement slice: isolated runtime graphs now fail closed for browser, file, database/Redis, Docker, Git, statistics/process monitors, agent providers, and MCP-backed agent work instead of constructing their host-owned backends. The behavior applies to saved definitions, recovery, saved connection launches, connection replacement, and agent layout mutations. Integration coverage proves an isolated workspace opens its terminal through the isolation runtime while non-terminal host factories and the agent runtime are not instantiated. Actual support for these clients still requires the per-workspace guest session host/RPC boundary described above; this issue remains in progress for that implementation and workspace networking.
Deep-review design proposal (not yet selected for implementation): replace isolation-only panel-service branching with a provider-neutral workspace runtime/services lease created for every workspace. A workspace network runtime should prepare direct/proxy/VPN/tailnet policy against an optional isolation binding and expose typed HTTP/SOCKS routing, terminal environment, capabilities, and cleanup. Remove the capability-only WorkspaceNetworkAttachment flag unless/until an operation exists. Cover plain/isolated × direct/proxy/VPN with agent-host/agent-workspace matrix tests. Relay hardening is tracked in asura-e53.
2026-09-02 architecture slice: replaced isolation-only panel services with provider-neutral WorkspaceRuntimeServices acquired for every workspace. The lease carries selected session/file/database/Redis/Docker/Git/browser backends plus a direct, proxy, or adapter-attached network route and a single cleanup lifetime. Removed the capability-only WorkspaceNetworkAttachment flag. Plain and isolated routes now share the extension point needed by the future per-workspace proxy/VPN/tailnet runtime; actual policy adapters and the full routing matrix remain in progress.
2026-09-02 follow-up after browser initialization regression: browser and terminal panel sessions remain on the window's registered session graph while workspace adapters own command execution and renderer routing. Removed the desktop adapter's isolate-local in-process system-monitor session host because it never receives the workspace graph and therefore cannot legally host panel sessions. WorkspaceRuntimeBackends.SystemMonitorSessionClient is now an explicit optional slot; isolated monitors fail closed until this issue adds the planned guest/RPC session host.

Desktop composition routes factory creation to a workspace-lifetime, isolation-command-backed monitor factory. This supports monitor panels now without a second unregistered session host; remaining proxy/VPN/tailnet policy adapters and routing matrix stay in scope.

title: Investigate gVisor IPv4 forwarding header lifetime race in native gateway
description: The unchanged native gateway race check intermittently fails TestEthernetRoutesTCPUDPAndDNS/ipv4-proxy-address/tcp-100.64.0.1. One goroutine allocates a pooled buffer in router_test.go inject (line 303); another reads IPv4.TTL at pinned gVisor ipv4.go:802 via router.go injectMarked. Investigate and validate an upstream fix or a narrow ownership boundary fix with repeated race tests and full native routing coverage. Do not suppress the race detector or serialize tests to hide it.
